subject.title: feat(telegram): auto-render simple options as inline buttons

question: Should OpenClaw support automatic conversion of free-form trailing `Options:` text into Telegram callbacks, or require all interactive controls to be declared through the existing explicit typed button payload?
rationale: This chooses a durable user-facing presentation and callback contract, including whether ordinary generated text may be reinterpreted and removed by one channel adapter; the branch cannot safely make that product decision alone.

options.title: Keep explicit button payloads
options.body: Reject raw-text inference and route interactive Telegram controls through the existing `buttons` payload or a typed upstream action.

options.title: Adopt a typed cross-channel action
options.body: If automatic option UI is a product goal, define an owner-approved structured presentation action with documented fallback behavior before adapting it to Telegram.

options.title: Accept the Telegram heuristic
options.body: Intentionally document `Options:` as a Telegram-specific reserved trailing syntax and own its upgrade and cross-channel behavior.

recommendation.title: Keep explicit button payloads
recommendation.body: Reject raw-text inference and route interactive Telegram controls through the existing `buttons` payload or a typed upstream action.

likelyOwner.reason: lntutor can clarify the proposal's intended semantics while a current-main Telegram feature owner is identified for the product decision.
